He attended [[Princeton High School (Ohio)|Princeton High School]] in [[Sharonville, Ohio]] after playing his first two years at [[Finneytown High School]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the top prospect in his state, earning [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] honors in [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]. Bazley initially committed to and signed with [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] but later chose to bypass college with intentions of joining the [[NBA G League]], a decision that drew national attention.{{cite web|title=Syracuse commit Darius Bazley to jump to G League|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/projected-top-10-draft-pick-make-leap-high-school-g-league-193725979.html|publisher=[[Yahoo!]]|accessdate=30 March 2018}} However, he instead chose to train independently as an intern for [[New Balance]] throughout the season leading up to the [[2019 NBA draft]]. In the draft, he was selected 23rd overall by the [[Utah Jazz]] before immediately being traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and then to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Bazley spent four seasons with the Thunder before being traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2023. ==High school career== Bazley began playing high school basketball at [[Finneytown High School]] in [[Springfield Township, Hamilton County, Ohio|Springfield Township, Ohio]]. He was ruled ineligible for the first half of his freshman season.{{cite web |last=Baum |first=Adam |last2=Robbe |first2=Nick |title=Roger Bacon basketball looking to reload |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2014/11/28/roger-bacon-basketball-looking-reload/19631365/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=August 12, 2018 |date=November 28, 2014}} As a sophomore, Bazley started drawing interest from several college programs, including [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].{{cite web |last=Schmetzer |first=Mark |title=Finneytown's Bazley handles spotlight, roundball |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2015/12/22/finneytowns-bazley-handles-spotlight/77772006/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=August 12, 2018 |date=December 22, 2015}} On December 19, 2015, he posted 25 points, 15 rebounds, and 5 blocks against [[Woodward Career Technical High School|Woodward High School]]. After averaging 15.8 points, 12.4 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.4 blocks and 1.5 steals, he was named to the Division III Southwest Ohio all-district second team.{{cite web |date=March 3, 2016 |title=SW Ohio All-District boys hoops teams named |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2016/03/03/sw-ohio-all-district-boys-hoops-teams-named/81261620 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]}}{{cite web |last=Dyer |first=Mike |title=Finneytown's Darius Bazley is ranked Ohio's No. 1 player in the 2018 class |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/insider/finneytowns-darius-bazley-is-ranked-the-states-no-1-player-in-the-2018-class |publisher=[[WCPO-TV]] |access-date=August 12, 2018 |date=June 20, 2016}} Entering his junior campaign, Bazley was the top-ranked player in Ohio. In July 2016, it was announced that he would transfer to [[Princeton High School (Ohio)|Princeton High School]] in [[Sharonville, Ohio]].{{cite web |last=Dyer |first=Mike |title=Finneytown basketball standout Darius Bazley transfers to Princeton |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/ohio-high-school-sports/finneytown-basketball-standout-darius-bazley-transfers-to-princeton |publisher=[[WCPO-TV]] |access-date=August 13, 2018 |date=July 30, 2016}} He was sidelined for his first 11 games because of transfer rules.{{cite web |title=Five things to know: Darius Bazley |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/03/hsum-features-bazley.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814040215/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2018/03/hsum-features-bazley.aspx |archive-date=August 14, 2018 |url-status=dead |access-date=August 13, 2018 |publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}} In August, Bazley committed to Ohio State, being rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]] at the time.{{cite web |last=Landis |first=Bill |title=Darius Bazley, Justin Ahrens -- pair of 2018 Ohio prospects -- commit to Ohio State basketball |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/index.ssf/2016/08/darius_bazley_justin_ahrens_--.html |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |access-date=August 13, 2018 |date=August 27, 2016}} On January 11, 2017, he debuted for Princeton, recording 11 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 steals in a loss at the Flyin' To The Hoop Invitational.{{cite web |last=Dyer |first=Mike |title=Princeton basketball standout Darius Bazley reflects on season debut ==Professional career== On March 30, 2018, Bazley announced that he would skip college with plans to join the [[NBA G League]] directly from high school.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Five-star recruit Darius Bazley to de-commit from Syracuse, join G League |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22958288 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 13, 2018 |date=March 30, 2018}} In April, he hired sports agent [[Rich Paul]] of Klutch Sports Group.{{cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |title=Darius Bazley Charts Yet Another Path to the N.B.A.: The Development League |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/23/sports/darius-bazley.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=August 13, 2018 |date=April 23, 2018}} Syracuse head coach [[Jim Boeheim]], who Bazley was expected to play under in college before the move, responded, "I hope he does great. But I don't think it's the way it will be. I think it will be proven it's not the way to get to the NBA."{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Dave |title=Boeheim on Bazley: 'It's not the way to get to the NBA' |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/04/04/boeheim-bazley-its-not-way-get-nba/485595002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |access-date=August 13, 2018 |date=April 4, 2018}} On August 27, Bazley announced that he would drop his G League plans altogether, opting instead to train on his own for the season.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |date=August 27, 2018 |title=Darius Bazley, the first top high school prospect to choose the G League over college, opts to train on his own instead |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/489209/2018/08/27/darius-bazley-scraps-g-league-move-to-train-on-his-own-ahead-of-nba-draft/ |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=The Athletic}} On October 25, he began a three-month internship with [[New Balance]] worth $1 million.{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2018 |title=Rich Paul: Darius Bazley's $1M internship a by-product of 'broken system' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25074140 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} After concluding his internship, Bazley became one of the first players to enter the [[2019 NBA draft]],{{Cite web |last=Bowers |first=Brendan |date=April 1, 2019 |title=Did Darius Bazley and Klutch Sports make the right call? |url=https://lebronwire.usatoday.com/2019/04/01/did-darius-bazley-and-klutch-sports-make-the-right-call |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=lebronwire.usatoday.com}}{{Cite web |date=April 23, 2019 |title=NBA announces early entry candidates for 2019 NBA Draft presented by State Farm |url=https://pr.nba.com/early-entry-candidates-2019-draft |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=pr.nba.com}} later being named one of 77 overall prospects invited to the 2019 [[NBA Draft Combine]].{{Cite web |date=May 19, 2019 |title=Sixty-six players expected to attend NBA Draft Combine |url=https://www.nba.com/news/66-players-attend-nba-draft-combine |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2019–2023)=== Bazley was drafted 23rd overall by the [[Utah Jazz]] but was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],{{cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Grayson Allen, Jae Crowder, Kyle Korver, draft rights to Darius Bazley and future first round draft pick from Utah Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-utah-jazz-trade-190706 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} who then traded him to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Thunder Acquires Draft Rights to Darius Bazley |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-bazley-190706 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On November 15, 2019, Bazley made his NBA debut, recording five points in a 127–119 overtime win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |last=Brunt |first=Cliff |date=November 16, 2019 |title=GALLINARI, PAUL LEAD THUNDER PAST 76ERS 127-119 IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900172 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On August 9, 2020, he scored a season-high 23 points, along with seven rebounds, in a 121–103 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |date=August 9, 2020 |title=THUNDER KEEP WIZARDS WINLESS IN BUBBLE WITH 121-103 WIN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021901285 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On April 19, 2021, Bazley logged a season-high 26 points, along with seven rebounds and three assists, in a 107–119 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |last=Nuckols |first=Ben |date=April 19, 2021 |title=BEAL, BERTANS LIFT WIZARDS PAST THUNDER FOR 5TH STRAIGHT WIN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000872 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Two days later, he matched this total alongside nine rebounds in a 116–122 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |last=Marot |first=Michael |date=April 21, 2021 |title=PACERS' SMALL BALL COMES UP BIG IN 122-116 WIN OVER THUNDER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000882 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On March 13, 2022, Bazley recorded a career-high 29 points, along with ten rebounds, in a 118–125 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |last=Martinez |first=Justin |date=March 13, 2022 |title=GRIZZLIES LEAD FOR ALL BUT 25 SECONDS IN WIN OVER THUNDER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101018 |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On March 28, he was ruled
